Question:
Does your company run a documented information security program that
senior management has approved?
Are your security policies reviewed at least annually?

Has your company assigned a named individual or team to own the
information security program?
Is your company certified to ISO/IEC 27001?

Do you hold a current SOC 2 Type II report from an independent
auditor?

Do you complete a documented security self-assessment of your product
at least annually?

Do employees reach your internal systems through a single sign-on
service?

Is multi-factor authentication required for all users, including
customer administrators of your product?

Do you review who has access to your internal systems at least
quarterly?

Is a leaver's access to your internal systems removed within 24 hours
of their departure?

Is access to internal systems granted by role and limited to what each
person needs for their job?
Do you enforce a minimum password length for employee accounts?

Does the owner of each system confirm at least quarterly that everyone
with access still needs it?

Do both your own staff and your customers' administrators have to use
multi-factor authentication to sign in?

Do you have an auditable process for granting and revoking physical
access to your office facilities?

Can your customers sign in to your product through single sign-on with
their own identity provider?
Is customer data encrypted at rest in your production environment?
Do you encrypt customer data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher?
Are your encryption keys rotated at least annually?

Do you have a data classification scheme that assigns each type of
data you handle a sensitivity level?
